answers.answer: Build the deck top to bottom from 1 randomly dealt Conflict I card, then 5 randomly dealt Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Shuffle each tier before dealing; return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: the top-to-bottom tier order and unused-card instruction.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 12 troops total, with 3 in the garrison and 9 in supply; 1 water; one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks. Starting VP is 0 in three-player play and 1 in four-player play.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 5–8: Agents, troop allocation, water and Influence; step 6: score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may Reveal while Agents remain. After Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase; you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue can be played only during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns, so you cannot play one later in the phase after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player Turns: Agent turns are optional; after Reveal, turns are skipped. Plot cards are playable during your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from hand face up and send one Agent to an unoccupied space whose icon matches one Agent icon on that card. One card sends only one Agent; a card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn. Meet requirements and pay required space costs immediately before resolving effects; if unable to pay, you cannot enter.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Agent turn: card/icon matching, one Agent, unoccupied space, and costs paid before resolving effects.

answers.answer: No. Conspire’s 4-spice entry cost is paid before effects of the played card or space, so an Agent-card spice gain cannot pay it when you start with only 3. After paying, resolve board-space effects, the card’s Agent box, and the one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs paid immediately before any effects; after payment, space, Agent box and Influence can resolve in any order. Board-space table: Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You can deploy at most 5 troops: all 3 recruited this turn plus up to 2 additional troops from the garrison. Any recruits not deployed remain in your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits go to the garrison and are not normally deployable there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn, Recruiting/Deploying: deploy any or all troops recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison; recruits not deployed go to garrison. Combat-space list excludes Rally Troops.

answers.answer: Reveal remaining hand; resolve Reveal boxes only on cards revealed now, in any order; set Combat strength; clean up by putting all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile. A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used during that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Reveal turn steps 1–4; Cleanup specifies cards from both Agent and Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Yes, the Imperium Row refills immediately and you may buy its replacement if affordable. Persuasion can be pooled from multiple sources for one card or split across different cards. Leftover Persuasion is lost and cannot be saved; acquired cards go to your discard pile and are not used immediately. An Acquire-box effect happens once when the card is acquired.
answers.evidence: Actions, Acquiring cards: immediate Row refill, pooling/splitting Persuasion, no saving, discard destination, and Acquire-box timing.

answers.answer: 3 troops are 6 strength and 4 revealed swords add 4, for 10 total. If your last troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased, even by swords. Above 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn, Set Strength: each Conflict troop is 2, each sword 1; no troops means 0; over 20 marker procedure.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and going clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing earlier does not prevent playing later. Combat resolves after all involved players pass consecutively. A 'when you win a Conflict' card is played only after winning, before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: order, troop eligibility, pass rule, resolution trigger and win-trigger timing.

answers.answer: A and B tied for first means nobody wins; each takes the second reward. C and D then compete for third; in a four-player game, the ordinary third-place finisher receives the third reward, so C gets it and D gets none. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in two- or three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. Zero strength receives nothing. After rewards, troops go to each player's supply, not garrison.
answers.evidence: Combat, Resolve Combat and Ties: first-place tie, four-player third reward, second/third-place tie rules, zero strength and troop destination.

answers.answer: Maker bonuses are placed in Phase 4: Makers, after Combat. Check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin and Imperial Basin; add 1 spice from the bank to each space with no Agent, accumulating with existing bonus spice. Normal harvesting occurs when a player sends an Agent to a Maker space: gain its listed base spice plus any bonus spice there. If an Agent moves away and the space is empty at Makers, it gets bonus spice then.
answers.evidence: Phase 4: Makers; Board spaces table lists base harvests; Maker spaces clarification says an empty space after an Agent moves away still accumulates bonus spice.

answers.answer: The game ends at the end of the round in Recall if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty; reaching 10 mid-round does not end it immediately. Resolve Endgame Intrigue before declaring the player with most VP the winner. Tiebreaks: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions and Phase 5: Recall give end trigger, Endgame resolution and full tiebreak order.

answers.answer: The VP at 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The 4-Influence track bonus is kept after dropping below 4 and may be earned again by dropping back and advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; an opponent takes it by rising to a higher track space, not merely tying the holder.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Faction Influence and Alliances.

answers.answer: If you drop from 5 while two opponents are tied with you, the former holder chooses one of those previously tied opponents to take the Alliance. If you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose it; with no other player at 4 or more, return it to the board.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Alliances: previously tied players are eligible after holder loses Influence; holder at 3 or less loses token, which returns if no one has 4+.

answers.answer: Discarding means a card from your hand unless specified otherwise; it goes to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard pile or in play to the box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect an empty deck's top card.
answers.evidence: Actions, Trashing cards; Special Rules, Deck exhaustion says you cannot reshuffle early to look at the top card.

answers.answer: Control of Arrakeen or Carthag pays its controller 1 Solari whenever any player, including the controller, sends an Agent there; Imperial Basin pays its controller 1 spice. Winning a Conflict rewarding control places your marker on that space’s flag, replacing any opponent marker. When a Conflict for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Control.

answers.answer: Use an unused color; put one cube at the bottom of each Influence track and remaining cubes in supply, with no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P; shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards and place the deck and its three Agents by its supply. After each First Player Agent turn, Hagal takes one Agent turn if it has an Agent left; it never Reveals. It does not collect resources, build a deck, earn Conflict rewards or score VP, and cannot claim Control; it can hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal Rival, Setup and Agent turns; opening paragraph states what it does not do and that it can hold Alliances.

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, reveal cards until an eligible unoccupied space appears; if a two-space card's currently applicable option is occupied, reveal another card and do not switch to the other option. Reshuffle immediately when the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears. Ignore space costs, requirements and effects; resolve only card icons/instructions. Troop icons recruit from supply; deploy recruits if the space is a Combat space, otherwise put them in garrison. On a Combat space, automatically deploy up to two additional garrison troops if available. Harvest Spice chooses the Maker with most bonus spice, ties by total (base plus bonus); if no bonus exists, reveal another card; return all bonus spice from the harvested space to the bank.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal Rival, Agent turns, troop rules and Harvest Spice procedure.

answers.answer: If Hagal has troops in the Conflict, reveal a House Hagal card in turn order, reshuffling and revealing again if it is Reshuffle; count its sword icons plus 2 strength per deployed troop. Humans then play Combat Intrigue before Combat resolves. Hagal receives no reward but occupies its rank. If it wins a space controlled by a human, remove that Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. Human ties for second receive the third reward even though an ordinary third-place finish pays nothing in a two-player game.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat strength procedure and reward/control rules; general Combat Ties section.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card and each player draws 5 cards. In non-ending Recall, return Mentat to its Landsraad space if needed, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise and start the next round. The Sort Through the Chaos winner takes the Mentat at the start of the next round.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start; Phase 5: Recall.

answers.answer: Solari, spice and water tokens are not limited; substitute if the bank runs out. If your supply has no troop cubes, you cannot recruit more until some troops return.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: resources are not limited; Agent turn, Recruiting: no supply troops means no further recruitment until some return.

answers.answer: Each Leader has a unique ability as described on the Leader, plus a Signet Ring ability activated when you play your Signet Ring card on one of your Agent turns. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Overview: Leader abilities and card override note.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr is a City-icon space requiring 2+ Fremen Influence; it recruits one troop and gains 1 water. It is a Combat space, so deployment is permitted. You cannot enter at 1 Influence and use the card effect to reach 2, because space requirements must be met before resolving effects.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table and Combat-space list; Agent turn says requirements/costs before effects.

answers.answer: Combat spaces are Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station, Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Heighliner, Hardy Warriors and Stillsuits. Research Station and The Great Flat are included; Conspire is not.
answers.evidence: Actions, Board spaces: complete list of Combat spaces.

answers.answer: Wealth (Emperor): no cost; +1 Emperor Influence and 2 Solari. Conspire (Emperor): 4 spice; +1 Emperor Influence, 5 Solari, recruit 2 troops, draw Intrigue. Foldspace (Spacing Guild): no cost; +1 Guild Influence and acquire a Foldspace card from Reserve. Heighliner (Spacing Guild): 6 spice; +1 Guild Influence, recruit 5 troops, gain 2 water. Secrets (Bene Gesserit): no cost; +1 Influence, draw Intrigue, each opponent with 4+ Intrigue gives you one at random. Selective Breeding (Bene Gesserit): 2 spice; +1 Influence, trash one card to draw two. Stillsuits (Fremen): no cost; +1 Influence, gain 1 water. Hardy Warriors (Fremen): 1 water; +1 Influence, recruit 2 troops.
answers.evidence: Actions, Board spaces table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen (City): no cost; recruit a troop and draw a card; its controller gets 1 Solari. Carthag (City): no cost; recruit a troop and draw Intrigue; controller gets 1 Solari. Research Station (City): 2 water; draw three cards. Secure Contract (Spice Trade): no cost; gain 3 Solari. Imperial Basin (Spice Trade): no cost; gain 1 spice plus bonus spice; controller gets 1 spice. Hagga Basin (Spice Trade): 1 water; gain 2 spice plus bonus. The Great Flat (Spice Trade): 2 water; gain 3 spice plus bonus.
answers.evidence: Actions, Board spaces table; Special Rules, Control gives controller bonuses.

answers.answer: Sell Melange uses the Spice Trade icon. Pay 2, 3, 4 or 5 spice to gain 6, 8, 10 or 12 Solari, respectively; one exchange per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions, Board spaces table: Sell Melange.

answers.answer: High Council costs 5 Solari, is once per game per player, and gives 2 Persuasion during each Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Swordmaster costs 8 Solari, is once per game per player, and gives your third Agent; you have three Agents for the rest of the game, including that round.
answers.evidence: Actions, Board spaces table: High Council and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Hall of Oratory has no cost, recruits one troop, and gives 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if you have an Agent there. Rally Troops costs 4 Solari and recruits four troops to garrison (it is not a Combat space). Mentat costs 2 Solari and draws a card; if Mentat is on that space, take it as an Agent for this round and return it at Recall.
answers.evidence: Actions, Board spaces table: Landsraad spaces.

answers.answer: Yes. A recalled Agent returns to your Leader and may be used on another Agent turn in that same round. This does not reopen turns after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Recall effects.

answers.answer: Fremen Bond works when you have at least one other Fremen card in play; cards played on Agent turns and revealed on Reveal remain face up in play until Cleanup unless trashed first. Two Fremen Bond cards enable one another regardless of play order.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: A single gain-two-Influence effect cannot be split between Factions. Alliance-icon effects require holding that Faction's Alliance; numeric-Influence icons require at least the shown Influence in that Faction.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Conditional icons.

answers.answer: Keep Intrigue cards face down, separate from your deck; you may inspect your own cards at any time and reveal them only when played. Played cards go face up beside the Intrigue Deck. Plot is played on your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat only during Combat; Endgame only at game end. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discards into a new deck. Costs and conditions must be met to play an Intrigue card.
answers.evidence: Actions, Intrigue cards; Agent-turn rules on Intrigue costs and conditions.

answers.answer: Yes. A delayed Plot such as Charisma or Recruitment Mission may be played during your Agent turn, left face up until that Reveal turn, then used and discarded.
answers.evidence: Actions, Intrigue cards: delayed Plot timing and disposal.

answers.answer: A card drawn during your Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used that turn; it cannot create an Agent turn. Cards drawn after your Reveal turn stay in hand for next round, when you also draw five additional cards.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn, Resolve Reveal Effects.

answers.answer: Most ordinary board/card effects are mandatory unless they say 'may,' are an optional arrow, or use optional black-X trashing. An ordinary card's optional arrow payment/effect may be declined; board entry costs must be paid, and Intrigue costs/conditions must be met. Standalone black-X trash is optional; trash used to pay a cost is required for that cost's effect; a non-arrow instruction to trash the card itself is mandatory. An optional arrow effect can be paid and resolved only once, not repeated by paying again.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: optional and mandatory effects, costs, trashing, and one-time arrow rule.

answers.answer: Play Bindu Suspension at the start of your Agent turn, before anything else; draw a card, then immediately end your turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Rulebook clarifications: Bindu Suspension.

answers.answer: Calculated Hire can take the Mentat only from its starting space in the Landsraad, not from another player or another space. For Sort Through the Chaos, take the Mentat at the start of the next round and use it that round.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Mentat; Rulebook clarifications, Calculated Hire and Mentat reward.

answers.answer: Kwisatz Haderach can allow an Agent turn with no unused Agents by sending an Agent already on a board space, even back to the same space. It cannot reuse once-per-game High Council or Swordmaster, and cannot overcome The Voice.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Rulebook clarifications: Kwisatz Haderach.

answers.answer: The Voice marks the chosen space with one of your available Control markers; remove it on your next turn. It stops opponents, including through Kwisatz Haderach, from sending Agents there for one turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Rulebook clarifications: The Voice.

answers.answer: Affected opponents choose their own cards to discard from their own hands, resolving opponents starting from your left and proceeding clockwise. For Test of Humanity, each opponent must choose something they can actually do: no discard from an empty hand and no losing a deployed troop they do not have.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Rulebook clarifications: opponent discards — Test of Humanity and Reverend Mother Mohiam.

answers.answer: After completing setup and before the first round, Baron Vladimir Harkonnen secretly chooses two of the four tokens and places them Faction-side down on the Leader; return the other two to the box unseen. Reveal them later to gain the reward, only once per game.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Rulebook clarifications: Baron Vladimir Harkonnen (Masterstroke).

answers.answer: Yes. If you win a Conflict that rewards spice, you may take that spice first and use it to play Demand Respect; To the Victor… can likewise fund it. A win-trigger Intrigue drawn as a victory reward may be played immediately. A win-trigger card cannot be played on a first-place tie because nobody won.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Demand Respect clarification; Combat Ties section on win-trigger cards.

answers.answer: Yes, zero is allowed when an effect says retreat any number. Retreated troops move from Conflict to garrison; lost troops return to supply.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Losing vs. retreating troops.

answers.answer: No. Assassination Mission does not trash itself for its 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws Intrigue only when its own self-trash effect is used, not when another effect trashes it.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Assassination Mission / Imperial Spy.

answers.answer: Yes, keep the VP from acquiring The Spice Must Flow if it is later trashed. Guild Bankers' discount applies to each copy acquired that turn.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers.

answers.answer: Count The Spice Must Flow cards in your deck and discard pile. Compare each opponent separately: for the second condition, you must have more than every opponent; if any one has at least as many, you fail that condition.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Corner the Market.

answers.answer: Ruthless Negotiator triggers only when paying the printed Solari cost of a board space, not a card ability that costs Solari. Ariana's Spice Addict is mandatory and applies only to spice harvested by sending an Agent to a Maker space, not spice gained by other means.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Count Ilban Richese / Countess Ariana Thorvald.

answers.answer: Original base spice is 1 at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin and 3 at The Great Flat; bonus spice is separate from base. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards from your Agent turns this round and your current Reveal turn, giving 2 Persuasion per such card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Carryall / Liet Kynes.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the set-aside card. You may acquire it through another effect, but the 1-Persuasion discount does not apply then. If not acquired by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Helena Richese — Manipulate.

answers.answer: Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but does not require a troop in your own supply. Gun Thopter's Agent box does not affect an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Double Cross / Gun Thopter.

answers.answer: Shifting Allegiances may lose and gain Influence with the same Faction for a net gain of one, but must actually pay the one-Influence loss; a Faction at zero cannot pay it. Each Influence track has six spaces; 3 Influence is immediately above the 2-Influence VP space.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Shifting Allegiances; Special Rules, Faction Influence.

answers.answer: Recruitment Mission's acquisition destination choice applies only to cards acquired during your Reveal turn that round, not Agent-turn acquisitions. For each card acquired during Reveal, choose independently whether it goes atop your deck or into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Recruitment Mission.

answers.answer: Refocus reshuffles your deck if your discard pile is empty. Cards drawn during Reveal must immediately be revealed and used during that turn.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Refocus / Poison Snooper.

answers.answer: Missionaria Protectiva belongs to the Bene Gesserit Faction. After replacing misprints, include only two copies in the Imperium deck.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Missionaria Protectiva erratum.

answers.answer: Yes. You can score above 12 VP; the printed Score track end is not a limit.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: score above 12 is allowed.

answers.answer: House Hagal is affected by effects targeting opponents or players if it has the specified resources. It receives no Influence-track bonuses and its Signet Ring icons have no effect in two-player play (they are solo-only).
answers.evidence: House Hagal opening paragraph; Agent turns rules for Influence and Signet Ring.

answers.answer: House Hagal acts after each First Player Agent turn, not after the other human's turn or a Reveal turn. It can take up to three turns in a round, following the First Player's actual Agent turns and its available Agents; a Swordmaster can give the First Player a third Agent turn and allow Hagal a third turn. Temporary Mentat/recalled Agents can also add a turn; early Reveal can reduce the count.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Rival, Agent turns: timing, maximum, Swordmaster and actual-count clarification.

answers.answer: Ordinary Reveal-turn Persuasion cannot buy Foldspace. It requires an acquire-Foldspace icon, normally obtained from the Foldspace board space.
answers.evidence: Actions, Acquiring cards: Foldspace requires its acquire icon, not Persuasion.

answers.answer: You retain the existing City and Fremen icons, and Dispatch an Envoy adds only missing Faction icons. It does not create a duplicate Fremen icon.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Dispatch an Envoy.

answers.answer: Yes. On a Combat-space Agent turn, deploy any or all troops recruited that turn from any source, including Intrigue cards, plus up to two additional troops from garrison. You cannot count or re-recruit an existing garrison troop as recruited to bypass the two-troop limit.
answers.evidence: Agent turn, Deploying: recruits from any source and up to two more from garrison; cannot re-recruit garrison troops to evade limit.

answers.answer: Draw the one remaining deck card, then reshuffle the discard pile to form a new deck and continue drawing the other two. Cards still face up in play do not enter the discard pile until Cleanup, so they are not part of that reshuffle.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Deck exhaustion: reshuffle discard when unable to draw; Reveal turn Cleanup puts cards in play into discard.

answers.answer: Each human takes a Leader and color components, shuffles the standard 10-card starting deck and places it face down in supply; place two Agents on Leader and third beside board, set Score and Combat markers, place Influence cubes and troops, give each player 1 water. Put Mentat on its side in its Landsraad space and Alliance tokens on track marks. Shuffle Intrigue deck face down; shuffle Imperium deck face down and deal five face-up Row cards; set Arrakis Liaison, The Spice Must Flow and Foldspace in separate Reserve stacks beside Row. Randomly choose initial First Player and give them the marker. Conflict setup is the separate tiered procedure.
answers.evidence: Components and Setup, steps 1–9; card-area instructions in step 3.

answers.answer: Unused components and supply pieces should be in clear view of all players. Intrigue cards remain face down and separate; their faces are not made public by the visible supply.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: supply components in clear view; Actions, Intrigue cards: keep face down and reveal only when played.

answers.answer: You may spend Persuasion to acquire cards before, between or after resolving Reveal effects; you need not finish all effects first.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn, Resolve Reveal Effects: acquire before, between or after Reveal effects.

answers.answer: City icon: Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station. Landsraad: High Council, Swordmaster, Hall of Oratory, Rally Troops, Mentat. Spice Trade: Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Secure Contract, Sell Melange.
answers.evidence: Actions, Agent icons and Board spaces: icon grouping and complete group lists.

answers.answer: Phase 2 begins with the holder of the First Player marker, then proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. Players take Agent turns or Reveal turns; a player may Reveal while Agents remain, after which their turns are skipped. The phase ends when every player has taken a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player Turns.

answers.answer: In three-player combat, 8 strength wins the top reward and 6 gets the second reward; the 4-strength ordinary third-place finisher gets no reward. In four-player play, an ordinary third-place finisher gets the third reward.
answers.evidence: Combat, Resolve Combat: first/second rewards and ordinary third reward only in four-player game.

answers.answer: If Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, it reveals a House Hagal combat card first in turn order; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again to obtain a combat card before counting swords. Humans then may play Combat Intrigue cards. If Hagal has no troop in the Conflict, it does not perform this strength-card reveal.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat strength procedure: conditional on at least one troop; reveal/reshuffle procedure; humans play after.

answers.answer: Corner the Market scores 1 VP for having at least two The Spice Must Flow cards and a separate 1 VP for having more than each opponent. The conditions score independently, so either alone scores 1 VP and both score 2. Count cards in your deck and discard pile; if any opponent has at least as many as you, you fail the second condition.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Corner the Market.

answers.answer: Yes. Sardaukar Legion's Reveal box can deploy up to three troops from your garrison during Reveal effects. Resolve it before Set Strength, so deployed troops count toward strength immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn: specific card effects can deploy; Sardaukar Legion example and timing.

answers.answer: Landsraad Popularity discounts the printed entry cost of a Landsraad (green) space by 1 Solari when Duke Leto sends an Agent there; apply the discount before paying. Prudent Diplomacy optionally pays 1 spice for 1 Influence in a Faction where an opponent has more Influence than Leto; a tie with no opponent ahead is not eligible.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Duke Leto Atreides.

answers.answer: Choose the Maker space with the most bonus spice; break a tie by total spice (base plus bonus). If none has bonus spice, reveal another House Hagal card. Remove all bonus spice from the chosen space and return it to the bank; Hagal keeps none.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Rival, Harvest Spice procedure.

answers.answer: Choose two different Factions and gain 1 Influence with each; you cannot choose the same option twice or put both into one Faction. This specific 'Choose two' differs from the generic gain-two icon, which also cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Conditional icons: Machinations chooses two different Factions; one gain-two effect cannot be split.

answers.answer: Master Tactician's '3 swords OR retreat up to 3 troops' offers alternatives; one play gives only one option. If retreating, move the troops from the Conflict to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Actions, Intrigue cards: Master Tactician example; Special Rules, Losing vs. retreating troops.
